title: CEO Interview with Moshiel Biton of Addionics
gist: Addionics CEO Moshiel Biton (the text spells his name Moshiel, unlike the title) pitches 3D porous metal current collectors that improve battery performance across chemistries and fit existing production lines, targeting autonomous fleets, defense, space and AI-infrastructure storage. The interview is promotional, with no quantified performance data beyond $85M raised.

themes.theme: Battery architecture as a physics-led approach

insights.claim: Addionics replaces flat metal current collectors with engineered three-dimensional porous structures, which it describes as bringing semiconductor-style precision design to batteries.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Cell-architecture innovation rather than new chemistry is the company's angle.
insights.quote: I often say we are bringing semiconductors to the battery industry.

insights.claim: Much of the battery industry focuses on chemistry while Addionics focuses on physics, aiming to complement different chemistries rather than depend on one winning: 'While others are betting on a horse, we are betting on the race.'
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Chemistry-agnostic enabling technology reduces exposure to any single chemistry winner.
insights.quote: While others are betting on a horse, we are betting on the race.
insights.locator: What does the competitive landscape look like

insights.claim: Addionics says its products are designed to integrate into existing battery production lines, which is central to its industrial differentiation.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Drop-in compatibility lowers adoption barriers for cell makers.

insights.claim: Addionics has raised over $85 million and established the world's first manufacturing facility for its 3D Current Collectors.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Indicates moderate funding and early manufacturing, but no revenue data.

themes.theme: Autonomy and physical AI power demand

insights.claim: As AI moves into autonomous vehicles, robotics, defense and space, batteries must enable sustained operation, repeated fast charging and continuous running with minimal rest.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Physical AI makes battery performance a bottleneck, not just compute.
insights.quote: The autonomous era demands sustained power, repeated fast charging, and continuous operation with minimal rest.

insights.claim: For autonomous fleets, charging downtime means lost revenue, so better batteries directly improve unit economics.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Charge time is an economic variable for robotaxi and robotics operators.
insights.locator: What keeps your customers up at night?

insights.claim: In space, battery failure can end an otherwise viable satellite's mission, while longer battery life can add years of service and revenue from the same asset.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Battery life shapes satellite asset economics.

insights.claim: Addionics sees strong potential in energy storage for AI infrastructure, where power delivery, reliability and lifetime matter.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: AI data center storage is a stated adjacent market without evidence of traction.

insights.claim: In defense, battery power, endurance and reliability affect mission success, with the author claiming better batteries can help determine who wins on the battlefield.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Defense drones and systems add a non-economic demand driver.

insights.claim: Addionics' Autonomous Architecture targets 24/7 operation with repeated charge-discharge cycles and little rest, and its Low-Temperature Architecture has shown promising cold-condition improvements that may reduce battery heating needs.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Product claims are qualitative with no disclosed metrics.
insights.locator: What new features or technology are you working on?

insights.claim: Customers engage by starting from performance targets and production constraints, then move through product samples, cell evaluation and qualification toward commercial supply.
insights.speaker: Moshiel Biton
insights.so_what: Qualification-based sales cycles imply long lead times before revenue.
insights.locator: How do customers normally engage with your company?
